description:
***About FHI 360***

FHI 360 is a nonprofit human development organization dedicated to improving lives in lasting ways by advancing integrated, locally driven solutions. Our staff includes experts in health, education, nutrition, economic development, youth, research, technology, communication, and social marketing—creating a unique mix of capabilities to address today’s interrelated development challenges. FHI 360 serves more than 60 countries and all U.S. states and territories.

***Job Summary:***

The Technical Director – HIV will provide overall technical leadership and direction for FHI 360’s HIV/AIDS technical assistance activities in India. Headquartered in New Delhi, India, the Technical Director will lead the planning, implementation, and technical oversight of activities designed to strengthen HIV case finding, reducing AIDS-related deaths, eliminating vertical transmission and sustaining epidemic control, along with integration with other health priorities. Working under the leadership of the AFGHS Project Director, the Technical Director – HIV will have primary responsibility for ensuring the technical quality and effective implementation of FHI 360’s HIV/AIDS portfolio, including oversight and mentoring of HIV technical personnel and consultants and coordination of technical activities, work plans, and associated budgets. The Technical Director - HIV will lead the development and implementation of annual and activity-specific work plans, monitor progress against established objectives and deliverables, identify and address implementation challenges, and ensure activities are completed on schedule and within approved budgets.

The Technical Director – HIV will serve as a principal technical liaison for FHI 360’s HIV activities with the National AIDS Control Organization (NACO) under the Government of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the U.S. Department of State partners, and other organizations supporting HIV/AIDS technical assistance in India. The Technical Director -HIV will promote strong coordination and alignment with government priorities and partner activities while identifying opportunities to leverage and integrate FHI 360’s broader health programming and technical capabilities. The position will support assessments, capacity strengthening, and technical assistance to national and subnational counterparts; provide oversight for high-quality technical, programmatic, and financial reporting; and ensure that FHI 360’s HIV activities are evidence-based, responsive to identified epidemiological and programmatic gaps, and implemented in accordance with donor requirements, FHI 360 policies, and national priorities.

***Accountabilities:***

The Technical Director-HIV works in close collaboration with the FHI 360 headquarters (HQ) technical team, planning and directing technical strategies and implementation of projects. S/he will lead the country HIV project team in the planning of project activities until completion of the project.

* Support rapid start-up of HIV activities in country, in alignment with donor and NACP priorities.
* Provide technical leadership to the HIV country team and liaise with AFGHS-HIV leadership at the global level to define, develop, implement, monitor and adjust technical work plans, presentations, and reports.
* Provide technical leadership in liaising with NACO, State AIDS Control Societies (SACS), and other relevant national and sub-national institutions in achieving project priorities through above-site and catalytic technical assistance.
* Ensure alignment of the HIV technical assistance priorities through annual work planning based on NACP priorities, epidemiological and programmatic evidence, transition needs, and available resources.
* Actively support in implementation oversight, performance monitoring and technical quality of HIV services as prioritized in the approved AFGHS workplan.
* Support national policy development, program optimization, performance monitoring, and quality improvement initiatives as planned under NACP and AFGHS Project.
* Contribute towards epidemic control preparedness, health system coordination, and multistakeholder collaboration across government departments, development partners, and civil society.
* Actively engage in development and adaptation of modules and guidelines on ART optimization, innovative case finding, index testing, pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP/PreP), HIV counselling and testing services, STI management, differentiated service delivery, and treatment literacy, as per requirement of the national program.
* Provide HIV care and treatment related technical and management support to HIV facilities and implementing partners under NACP to strengthen case management services, ensure ART initiation and strengthen viral load suppression through innovative, evidence-based programming.
* Remain informed on current state-of-the-art technical updates in HIV care and treatment through review of literature and articles and maintains link with other international bodies which specialize in at-risk population focused HIV treatment care and support.
* Ensure that the project technical deliverables meet or exceed quality standards. Ensure on-time delivery of high-quality deliverables and reports.
* Responsible for onboarding project staff and ensuring their familiarity with organizational and project mandate, values, quality standards, policies and objectives and their individual responsibilities in upholding these standards and policies.
* Support performance management and professional development of direct reports, including ongoing feedback, coaching, and career support.
* Ensure financial and contractual compliance with FHI 360 and donor rules and regulations.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Project Director, or as requested from the leadership of the national program.

**Qualifications and Experience**

* MBBS degree and master’s degree in public health, epidemiology and other related areas would be an added advantage.
* Minimum 15 years of progressively responsible experience in HIV program at the national level, preferably in HIV/AIDS service delivery including design and implementation of customized projects that fit within the country strategic plans and partnership frameworks.
* In-depth technical knowledge and experience of the NACP and the gaps and challenges in meeting the 95:95:95 goals
* Demonstrated experience in managing and leading teams of donor-funded projects.
* Experience working collaboratively with government institutions (especially NACO and SACS), INGOs, and multilateral organizations.
* Highly proficient with MS Project, and the Microsoft suite of programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Visio).
* Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
* Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills.

***The expected hiring salary range for this role is INR 3,000,000 - 5,000,000 for annual gross salary (basic and allowances). When determining an offer amount, FHI 360 factors in multiple considerations, including but not limited to: relevant years of experience and education possessed by the applicant, internal equity, market pay, and*** ***budget. For*** ***internal candidates, salary placement will also follow FHI 360’s current promotional increase guidelines.***

This document should not be construed in any way to represent a contract of employment. Management reserves the right to review and revise this document at any time.

FHI 360 takes steps to safeguard the welfare of everyone who engages with our organization and programs and requires that all personnel, including staff members and volunteers, share this commitment and sign our code of conduct. All offers of employment will be subject to appropriate screening checks, including reference, criminal record and terrorism finance checks. FHI 360 also participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), facilitated by the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response. In line with the MDS, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any substantiated findings of sexual abuse, exploitation and/or harassment during the applicant’s tenure with previous employers. By applying, job applicants confirm their understanding of these recruitment procedures and consent to these screening checks.

Reference code: DO/NCR-11/26

The International Forum for Environment, Sustainability & Technology (iFOREST) is looking for an experienced and dynamic leader to build and head the organisation’s people and operations functions, covering HR, administration and IT, across its three offices.

A successful applicant must have a proven record of leading HR functions, building HR policies, systems and teams in a growing organisation, and advising senior leadership on organisation design and workforce planning, and good communication skills with researchers, managers, and external agencies. The candidate should ideally have work experience in a think tank, non-profit or international NGO.

#### **Position summary**

**Title**

Director – People & Operations

  

**Reports to**

Chief Executive Officer

  

**Direct reports**

Manager – Culture & People; Manager – Talent Aquisiton, Manager – Operations

  

**Location**

Noida head office

  

**Experience**

20+ years in HR, with significant exposure to administration, including at least 10 years leading a function

  

**Remuneration**

Depending upon qualification and experience

#### **About iFOREST**

iFOREST is an independent, not-for-profit research and innovation organisation established in 2019. It identifies, promotes and scales up solutions for pressing environment–development challenges in India and other developing countries in Asia and Africa.

Our work is rooted in regional priorities. We accelerate environmental action at the sub-national level and use that regional knowledge to improve national policies and plans and strengthen international collaboration. We conduct independent, evidence-based research, develop new knowledge and innovative solutions, convene stakeholders to build consensus, and partner with think tanks, civil society, government agencies, philanthropies and industry to scale up solutions.

Much of our work is funded by international grants and delivered with state and district partners. We have a team of about 80 people across three offices in India.

#### **Purpose of the role**

The Director – People & Operations will build and lead iFOREST’s HR and administration support functions. HR is the primary focus of the role. The Director is a member of the senior management team and a close adviser to the CEO.

iFOREST is a young organisation, and many of its policies, SOPs and systems are evolving. A key aim is to take day-to-day HR and administrative work off the senior management, so they can focus on research, programmes and partnerships.

Success in this role means that, within a year:

* iFOREST has an approved, legally compliant and implementable set of HR and administrative policies, SOPs and delegations that staff understand, and managers apply consistently.
* Hiring keeps pace with new grants, and the organisation attracts and retains strong research and programme staff.
* Staff costs, contracts, records and procurement meet the requirements of donors and auditors without last-minute effort.
* The CEO is no longer involved in routine HR and administrative decisions.

#### **Key responsibilities**

Roughly 70% of the role is HR, and 30% is administration and IT oversight.

#### **1. HR and Administration leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the HR and administration Team, setting clear goals and standards of service.
* Build a service culture in which staff in every office know whom to contact and get timely answers.

#### **2. Strategy, policy and organisation design**

* Develop a people and operations strategy aligned with iFOREST’s mission, growth plans and values, in consultation with the CEO and senior management.
* Write, obtain approval for and ensure roll out the HR manual, administration manual, IT policy and the SOPs that sit under them, in line with good practice and applicable law.
* Propose a delegation of financial and administrative authority.
* Advise the CEO and senior management on organisation design, role levels, grading, spans of control and workforce planning.
* Prepare and manage the annual budget for HR, administration and IT, and track spending against it.

#### **5. Talent acquisition and onboarding**

* Plan staffing with programme heads for ongoing and new grants, including staffing assumptions for proposals.
* Lead recruitment at all levels: senior leadership, researchers, programme and field staff, fellows, interns, consultants and support staff.
* Set up fair, documented hiring processes, from job descriptions and sourcing to interview panels, reference checks and offers.
* Build iFOREST’s employer brand with universities, professional networks and peer institutions.
* Run structured onboarding and induction, including for staff joining regional offices.

#### **6. Performance, learning and careers**

* Run the annual performance cycle, including goal setting, probation reviews and feedback.
* Develop role levels, competencies, promotion criteria and career paths.
* Identify learning needs and lead training, mentoring and capacity building.
* Support leadership development and succession planning for critical roles.

#### **7. Compensation, benefits, payroll and grant compliance**

* Maintain a salary structure and benefits that are competitive in the think-tank and development sector, and administer leave and other benefits as per the company policies.
* Coordinate monthly payroll inputs and statutory deductions with the Finance team to ensure accuracy and timeliness.
* Work with Finance and programme teams on charging staff costs to grants, timesheets and effort reporting, and donor rules on salaries, consultants and benefits.
* Respond to the HR and administration sections of donor due-diligence reviews and audits.

#### **8. Employee relations, safeguarding and compliance**

* Develop, review, and update the HR manual, administrative manuals, guidelines, and SOPs in line with industry best practices and applicable laws.
* Ensure compliance with Indian labour and employment laws across all three offices, including state-specific registrations and returns.
* Ensure compliance with the POSH Act, including a functioning Internal Committee, awareness sessions and annual reporting.
* Develop and run a safeguarding policy and code of conduct that meets the expectations of iFOREST’s international donors, covering staff, consultants and partners working in communities.
* Oversee employment contracts, consultant and fellowship agreements, vendor service level agreements (SLAs), and official institutional documentation.
* Manage grievances, disciplinary matters and exits fairly, consistently and confidentially, including full-and-final settlements and analysis of attrition.
* Ensure personal data of staff is held securely and in line with data protection law.

#### **9. Culture, engagement and inclusion**

* Build an open, collaborative and mission-driven culture across head office and regional offices.
* Promote diversity, equity and inclusion in hiring, pay and progression.
* Lead staff wellbeing and duty of care, especially for field and regional staff who travel.

#### **10. Administration and facilities**

* Oversee office management, facilities, security and maintenance at head office and regional offices.
* Set up procurement and vendor management that is cost-effective and meets donor procurement rules.
* Oversee asset registers, insurance and annual physical verification.
* Oversee travel, logistics, events and support for workshops and visiting delegations, including visas and protocol for international guests.
* Oversee health, safety and business continuity plans for all offices.
* Make sure the CEO and senior management receive reliable administrative support, so they are freed from day-to-day administrative matters.

#### **11. IT and digital systems**

* Set direction for IT infrastructure, user support, information security and backups across all offices.
* Oversee selection and roll-out of HR, payroll and administrative systems (HRMS and MIS).
* Ensure IT policies, licences and data handling meet donor and legal requirements.
  

#### **Key relationships and authority**

**Relationship**

**Nature of work**

**CEO**

Reports to; adviser on people, organisation and operations matters

  

**Senior management and programme heads**

Partner on workforce planning, hiring, performance and team issues

  

**Finance**

Partner on payroll, budgets, staff-cost allocation to grants, procurement, audits

  

**Grants and programme teams**

Staffing in proposals, donor HR and procurement clauses, due diligence

  

**Regional office leads**

Delivery of HR, administration and IT services in each office

  

**Board or its committees**

Reports on people matters, policies and compliance as required

  

**External**

Legal and statutory advisers, auditors, insurers, recruitment partners, vendors, labour authorities

The Director will have authority, within approved policies, budgets and the delegation of authority, to approve routine HR, administrative and IT decisions.

#### **Qualifications and experience**

**Essential**

* Master’s degree in human resource management, personnel management, business or public administration, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
* 20+ years of progressive HR experience, with significant responsibility for administration, including at least 10 years leading an HR or operations function.
* End-to-end experience across recruitment, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations and compliance.
* Experience managing staff and services across more than one location.
* Experience building HR policies, systems and processes in a new or fast-growing organisation.
* Working knowledge of Indian labour laws and the POSH Act.

**Desirable**

* Experience in a think tank, research institution, non-profit, development organisation or international NGO.
* Experience with internationally funded grants, including donor rules on staff costs, procurement and safeguarding.
* Experience overseeing administration, procurement or IT functions.
* Experience introducing an HRMS or similar digital system.

**Competencies**

* Ability to turn organisational goals into practical people and operations plans.
* Writes clear policies and SOPs and gets them adopted.
* Builds trust with senior researchers, programme leaders and staff at all levels.
* Handles confidential and sensitive matters with integrity and discretion.
* Makes fair, consistent judgements in employee relations.
* Delegates well and develops a team, rather than doing the team’s work.
* Communicates clearly in English, in writing and in person.

#### **What we offer**

iFOREST provides an inclusive and supportive work environment and is committed to professional development through education, training and capacity building. We offer salaries that are competitive in the think-tank sector and recognise performance through annual appraisals.

Remuneration: Depending on qualifications and experience. The final designation will depend on the selected candidate’s qualifications and experience.

#### **How to apply**

Apply online at iforest.global/careers. If you have difficulty applying online, send your CV and a cover letter to careers@iforest.global with “Director – People & Operations” in the subject line.

Immediate opening. The position is open until filled.

Published

Nov 11, 2026

reference code in subject line.

* Purpose-driven work: Contribute from regional to national and global goals in
    
  sustainability.
* Professional development: Work in areas that address contemporary and critical issues.
* Competitive compensation: We recognize and reward commitment and talent.
* Inclusive culture: Experience a supportive, diverse, and empowering work environment.
